subject: object 'y' not found etc. Possible bug in Karmic

messages.author: 19597707260d4c7c
messages.subject: object 'y' not found etc. Possible bug in Karmic
parts:
Can anyone confirm a possible bug with (K)ubuntu Karmic default R/
ggplot2 and/or offer a workaround:

library(ggplot2)
qplot(mpg, data = mtcars) # this is from example(qplot), which thus
ends with error also

>stat_bin: binwidth defaulted to range/30. Use 'binwidth = x' to adjust this.
>Error in pmin(y, 0) : object 'y' not found

(setting binwidth to 1, 2, 3 does not help, giving an "object 'y' not
found" error)

the same with diamonds dataset (qplot(carat, data=diamonds,
geom="histogram") as is an example in the ggplot2 book). I had
revolution-r installed before, tried to remove everything and install
clean version (without revolution-r), but this behaviour remains.

It is possibly related with this post:
http://groups.google.com/group/ggplot2/browse_thread/thread/5c45f743c83825e0/a4fe652eedfca742?show_docid=a4fe652eedfca742
as I am also getting the "arguments imply different number of rows"
where (I think but am not sure) I should'nt.

I guess my options are either going back to jaunty or precompute
everything with plyr. But if it works for others, I will try to clean
and reinstall R again.

I were too quick to report it here. Upgrading r through r-cran
repository fixes the problem! Thus this bugreport should have been
adressed to ubuntu packagers.
Hope the post might help others in the same situation though - took a
newbie a long time to realize this was not my fault.
Indrek
